newsitem.title: USA: Palmdale and Lancaster, Calif., mull tax merger.
newsitem.headline: Palmdale and Lancaster, Calif., mull tax merger.

text.p: The southern California cities of Palmdale and Lancaster are considering an unprecedented plan to pool their future sales tax revenues, city officials said on Monday.
The plan, which is still being worked out and may require voter approval, calls for Palmdale and Lancaster to combine their sales tax revenues, and then split the proceeds evenly based on population.
The cities would, in turn, stop battling with each other for retailers, a costly practice of offering tax breaks, loans and other incentives to lure major businesses.
"The two cities are competing for the sales tax right now," said Palmdale City Manager Bob Toone. "It makes more sense just to split all the money, and not spend it on developers."
The tax sharing plan would reduce the amount spent by the cities to lure retailers and other businesses. The savings would be used to fund basic municipal services, Toone said.
The Palmdale-Lancaster plan, if carried out, would be unprecendented in California. Municipal credit analysts said the final plan would require a close review but could benefit both cities.

"It could be a positive," said Ken Kurtz, senior vice president at Moody's Investors Service Inc. "It could sort of end the competition that goes on between cities, and might help stabilize finances."

"It's innovative," added Standard & Poor's Corp Director Jeff Thiemann. Both cities could benefit "to the extent that they no longer have to compete with a neighbor for the same retail base," he said.
A public hearing on the Palmdale-Lancaster tax sharing proposal will be held in the coming weeks, Toone said. A date has not yet been set.
